items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names reveal intent (WindowFrameBoundary, assertPositiveInteger, buildWindowClause, addWindowDefinition). Public APIs have JSDoc, dprint was run on the changed files, and the formatting matches the existing aggregate.ts style.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Spec and validation logic lives once in window.ts (buildWindowClause/addWindowDefinition). Each dialect adds only an optional field, a thin .window() method and one chunk. window.ts is about 434 lines, under 500. The JSDoc for .window() is copied five times, which is minor.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Boundaries are validated: assertNonNegativeInteger/assertPositiveInteger include the function name and the received value, and frame ordering is checked. But one hidden test fails (F2P 129/130), so one specified edge case behaves differently from what was expected.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change is purely additive: `windows?: WindowDefinition[]` on all five configs, the same `window(name, spec): this` on pg/mysql/sqlite/singlestore/gel, and an `export * from './window.ts'`. Queries that don't use windows produce the same SQL as before, and all 566 P2P tests pass.
